class.name: WorldWater
class.brief_description: The water contract: open water of every kind, as the other world systems read it.
class.description: Answers for every live water producer at once (sea, rivers, pools, live water, standing water on the ground): each producer answers only where it really has water, and a point reads the surface nearest above it, else the nearest below it (so a cave stream or a pool in a hollow below the sea's level reads its own water). With no producer, [method height_at] is [code]-INF[/code] and the rest is still water. Get it from [WorldContracts]; a test extends it in a script and sets it with [method WorldContracts.set_water]. Units: metres, m/s, world space.

method.name: add_sediment
method.description: A suspended load entering the water that answers at [param position], in kg/s of mineral (silt and clay) and of ash and char: runoff off burnt or bare ground, a collapsing bank, a landslide. That water carries it on downstream and settles it. Where no water answers, it is dropped.

method.name: add_sediment_mass
method.description: A load dropped into the water that answers at [param position] at once, in kg of mineral and of ash: the fines of a debris flow or a landslide that stops in it, a bank's collapse. A river mixes it through the water around the point and carries it on; a lake through its whole volume. The load is capped at [code]1000[/code] kg/m³ (hyperconcentrated flow); a denser mixture is a debris flow. Where no water answers, it is dropped. For a load that keeps coming (runoff), use [method add_sediment].

method.name: breaking_at
method.description: Height of the waves breaking at [param position], in m, the largest any producer reports: the broken waves in a surf zone (about 0.78 of the depth), whitecap cover times wave height over open water, 0 where none break. Sea spray reads it ([method WorldWeather.sea_spray_at]).

method.name: clear
method.description: Ends the moving disturbance [param owner] keeps.

method.name: depth_at
method.description: How far [param position] lies under the water surface over it, in metres; 0 above it or with no water.

method.name: disturb
method.description: A body moving in the water at [param position]: ripples and wakes. [param owner] keeps one disturbance per body.

method.name: flow_at
method.description: The current of the water over [param position], in m/s; zero with no water.

method.name: has_provider
method.description: Whether any water producer is live.

method.name: height_at
method.description: The water surface for [param position] (world height in metres): of the producers with water there, the one nearest above it, else the nearest below; [code]-INF[/code] where there is none.

method.name: impulse
method.description: A single splash at [param position].

method.name: sediment_at
method.description: The suspended load of the water at [param position] (kg/m3): [code]x[/code] mineral, which clouds it brown, [code]y[/code] ash and char, which turn it grey to black. Both 0 for clear water or none.

method.name: wake_depth_at
method.description: How far the surface over [param position] is pushed down by wakes, in metres.

method.name: wave
method.description: An impulse wave in metres and seconds, from a landslide, an avalanche, calving ice or rockfall entering the water at [param position]: one crest and trough [param height] m high (crest to trough), [param period] s long, its crest [param width] m wide, setting off along [param direction]. Given to every producer with water there: [PhysXWaterSurface3D] carries it in its ripple solver ([method PhysXWaterSurface3D.submit_wave]), so it runs out at the long-wave speed, up the shores and back; a producer with no solver takes a splash of the crest's height ([method impulse]).
